comment: The CUDA pack: the three packages whose CUDA build differs from the bundle's CPU one, shipped
as byte-range parts of one zip. Produced by scripts/bundle-python-cuda.ps1 -Package, which
writes a manifest.json this file is filled in from. See docs/PHASES.md, 'Built 2026-08-29 --
the pack becomes a download' and 'Shipped 2026-08-29 -- the pack becomes a download that
exists'.
verified is TRUE as of v1.0.0-rc.8, and what that flag asserts is that the four parts exist at
baseUrl: the installer refuses an unverified manifest unless the caller opts in, on
ModelInstaller's terms, and that refusal is the only thing between a user and four 404s. These
digests are the ones scripts/bundle-python-cuda.ps1 -Package computed over the parts that were
then uploaded to that release, byte for byte. They were read back off the uploaded assets
afterwards rather than before, because the release cannot exist until the commit carrying this
file is tagged; docs/UNPROVEN.md records that read-back and its result. A pin taken from a
local build whose upload has NOT happened goes back to false.
The digests moved on 2026-08-29 without torch moving: a rebuild of the same pins produced a
zip 27,649 bytes larger than the one first recorded here, because requirements-bundle.txt pins
26 direct packages and nothing transitive. The pack is therefore not byte-reproducible, which
is why these are read off the artefact that shipped rather than assumed to match a rebuild.
The version is the bundle's own torch pin in its CUDA build. It must stay that way: the pack
shadows the bundle's torch by sitting ahead of it on PYTHONPATH, and a pack whose version has
drifted from python/requirements-bundle.txt would silently run a decode the translator's
8,149-sentence gate does not describe. CudaPackInstaller checks the pair at install.
